question: What are the candidate therapeutic targets and biomarkers in ccRCC with the strongest convergent evidence?

models.orchestrator: Claude Opus 5.5 (effort medium) — Claude Code main session
models.agents: Claude Sonnet 5.5 — Claude Code subagents (agente-omico, agente-literatura, agente-externo)

findings.statement: CA9 is up in all three layers: RNA log2FC 6.312 (padj 1.72e-49), protein log2FC 2.269 (padj 9.9e-43), phospho log2FC 1.91 (padj 5.18e-30). RNA-protein Spearman rho 0.797 (padj 6.48e-24); 9p loss frequency 0.145. A HIF-driven membrane enzyme, it is a strong tissue-biomarker and surface-target candidate.

CD70 is up in RNA (log2FC 4.464, padj 4.13e-35) and protein (log2FC 2.421, padj 1.94e-38), with RNA-protein rho 0.843 (padj 4e-29), the highest concordance among the candidates; CNV is minimal (gain 0.027, loss 0.009). A surface ligand with very large tumor-normal difference, consistent with an antibody/cell-therapy target.

EGFR is top of the convergence ranking (score 3.87, 5 streams). Up in RNA (log2FC 1.461, padj 1.76e-23), protein (log2FC 1.062, padj 7.32e-45) and phospho (log2FC 0.874, padj 1.99e-37); rho 0.699; 7p gain frequency 0.255. Effect sizes are modest but layer-concordant, with approved EGFR drugs available.

MET is up in RNA (log2FC 1.342, padj 1.19e-21), protein (log2FC 1.101, padj 1.42e-34) and phospho (log2FC 0.723, padj 8.03e-19); rho 0.817 (padj 5.62e-26); 7q gain frequency 0.255. Kinase activity signal supports MET as a druggable target (rank 6 in convergence).

COXFA4L2 (dataset symbol NDUFA4L2) has the largest tumor-normal change: RNA log2FC 6.752 (padj 1.66e-49), protein log2FC 3.768 (padj 5.99e-48), phospho log2FC 2.598; rho 0.634; 12q gain frequency 0.118. It is a hypoxia-driven mitochondrial gene, a top tissue biomarker rather than an obvious surface target.

NNMT is up in RNA (log2FC 4.67, padj 2.04e-40) and protein (log2FC 2.709, padj 1.23e-43); rho 0.634 (padj 6.46e-13); no marked CNV (loss 0.045, gain 0.027). Concordant across layers; metabolic enzyme with a small-molecule-inhibitor rationale and biomarker value.

PLIN2 is up in protein (log2FC 2.667, padj 7.99e-44), phospho (log2FC 1.9) and RNA (log2FC 2.62, padj 2.37e-26), reflecting lipid-droplet accumulation of ccRCC; RNA-protein rho is only 0.336 (padj 0.000618) and 9p loss frequency 0.164, so protein-level measurement is preferable.

ENO2 is up in RNA (log2FC 3.538, padj 4.81e-39), protein (log2FC 2.245, padj 2.91e-44) and phospho (log2FC 1.84); rho 0.716 (padj 1.78e-17); 12p gain frequency 0.118. Glycolytic marker consistent with the Warburg-like ccRCC phenotype.

SLC16A3 (MCT4, lactate exporter) is up in RNA (log2FC 3.435, padj 3.3e-49), protein (log2FC 2.279, padj 5.43e-47) and phospho (log2FC 1.48); membrane transporter with minimal CNV (gain 0.036, loss 0.018), a plausible metabolic target.

ALDOB is strongly down in RNA (log2FC -7.028, padj 9.42e-31), protein (log2FC -2.273, padj 2.07e-40) and phospho (log2FC -1.415), reflecting loss of proximal-tubule identity; a negative tissue biomarker, not a target. 9p loss frequency 0.164.

VHL sits on 3p with loss frequency 0.791 (gain 0.027) and is reduced in RNA (log2FC -0.479, padj 1.62e-17) and protein (log2FC -0.172, padj 0.04), the founding event behind HIF activation and the CA9/NDUFA4L2 signature. The protein change is small and borderline.

PBRM1 (3p) has copy-number loss frequency 0.8 (gain 0.027) with modest reductions in RNA (log2FC -0.238, padj 1.16e-08), protein (log2FC -0.265, padj 6.76e-12) and phospho (log2FC -0.246). Tumor-suppressor loss is a driver mechanism, not a directly targetable product.

caveats: CPTAC discovery cohort only (110 tumors; 75 RNA and 84 proteome/phosphoproteome matched normals); no independent validation was performed here.
Bulk tumor-vs-normal differences can reflect immune/stromal infiltration or tissue composition, not only tumor-cell expression.
Omics supports expression and copy number only; surface localization, druggability and safety were not assessed from these data beyond the convergence ranking.
Several cnv_frequency results (CA9, EGFR, MET, CD70, NNMT, PLIN2, ENO2, ALDOB, SLC16A3, COXFA4L2) have no evidence id, so CNV values are quoted without citation.
COXFA4L2 is the dataset symbol NDUFA4L2; EGFR/MET gains are arm-level 7p/7q events, not focal amplifications.

findings.statement: PMID:42473996: CA9 is preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumor cells with low normal-kidney expression; CA9-targeted PET offers proof-of-concept noninvasive discrimination of ccRCC, warranting prospective validation (single study, not validated clinically). High CA9 PET uptake associated with PBRM1 loss-of-function. PMID:35795483 reports CAIX mRNA increased in HIV-associated kidney cancer.

NDUFA4L2 is predictive of poor survival in ccRCC and supports proliferation/colony formation in cell lines (PMID:34970493); increases glycolysis (PMID:36722045); enhances lipid deposition and Ca9 expression in the TRACK early-ccRCC model; also a marker of low- and high-grade ccRCC in tissue and EVs (PMID:41656939).

PMID:36204178: MT1G downregulated in ccRCC vs normal tissue, proposed negative regulator of ferroptosis and poor-prognosis biomarker. PMID:38906969: high MT1G correlated with advanced stage and poorer prognosis; elevated MT1G promoted growth and metastasis in vitro/in vivo and inhibits CPT1B via H3K14 trimethylation, increasing lipid droplets. Note: tumour-vs-normal downregulation yet high expression is adverse within tumours.

SAP30 suppresses MT1G and the p53 pathway; SAP30 upregulated in ccRCC with poor prognosis; authors suggest SAP30 and MT1G as potential prognostic markers and therapeutic targets (PMID:40247376 and related chunks).

Chunks report MT1X as an oncogene indicating prognosis in ccRCC, an independent prognostic factor correlated with T/M stage and grade, with increased expression linked to worse prognosis (bioinformatic plus some experimental work).

PMID:37760940: ENO2 potential diagnostic biomarker and independent prognostic predictor in ccRCC, promoting progression via Warburg-effect glycolysis. PMID:39091581: ENO2 high in ccRCC cell lines; knockdown inhibits glycolysis and promotes ferroptosis. PMID:36313709: ENO2 related to OS. Enolase 2 also associated with TKI resistance (lenvatinib, cabozantinib) in cell lines.

PMID:40852386 reports ALDOB as a prognostic biomarker and potential immunotherapy target in ccRCC, linked to Treg/Th17/neutrophil infiltration; PMID:38655323 reports independent prognostic value in KIRC; PMID:37083815 pan-cancer low expression. Bioinformatic-heavy evidence.

PFKP upregulated in ccRCC (PMID:34321910, PMID:36901940); PMID:40341002 reports PFKP among glycolysis-related biomarkers with diagnostic and prognostic potential. PMID:34321910 notes low PFKP expression correlated with poor OS, which is direction-discordant with upregulation in tumour.
PLIN2 consistently upregulated in ccRCC (PMID:36901940), part of a diagnostic IHC panel validated on 128 samples (PMID:34482820) and related to prognosis via GEPIA (PMID:35314744).

PMID:41158242 (pan-cancer): ABAT underexpressed in KIRC and predicts poor prognosis in KIRC; PMID:41813748: ABAT overexpression suppresses tumour growth, mediates cGAS-STING and interacts with PRMT5 (context of that study not clear from sentence).

In ccRCC, ACY1 is only reported as downregulated (PMID:34002044, with MAGI2-AS3). Other relations concern colorectal cancer (oncogene, radiotherapy target in cetuximab-resistant CRC), so ccRCC therapeutic relevance is not supported.
PMID:34266404: CXCR4 and C3 overexpressed in ccRCC and associated with prognosis (database mining, single bioinformatic study).

Strong omics/tractability ranking (rank 2) but no literature relations; chunks describe CD74 expressed in both cancer cells and macrophages in ccRCC with a potential protumor function, with functional significance still unclear.

caveats: Top convergence genes (EGFR, FAS, PIGR, ERBB2, TNFRSF10B, ATP1A1, PDGFRA, KDR, EPAS1) have 0 literature relations in this corpus; literature is silent on them despite omics/Open Targets support. EGFR search returned no relevant EGFR sentences.

Clinically validated targets (HIF-2alpha inhibitor belzutifan; VEGFR TKIs/ICI combinations as standard of care) appear in chunks but only by alias (HIF-2alpha, VEGFR) and not as EPAS1/KDR symbols, so they are not cited as gene evidence.
Most literature-backed candidates (MT1G, MT1X, ENO2, ALDOB, PFKP, PLIN2, ABAT, COXFA4L2) rest on single or few bioinformatic/retrospective studies; none clinically validated as biomarker or target.

Contradictions: MT1G and PFKP are downregulated or upregulated in tumour vs normal yet high/low expression associated with adverse outcome in different studies; ACY1 evidence is mostly from colorectal cancer.
Corpus is ~320 abstracts; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

findings.statement: Open Targets association with ccRCC 0.4871 (rank 9 of 1998). Tractability: PR and SM (SM: Approved Drug). Drug: BELZUTIFAN (APPROVAL). Nuclear transcription factor (HIF-2alpha), regulates VEGF; Reactome HIF regulation and PD-L1 transcription. Convergence rank 38 (5 streams, ot_genetic_association 0.57, ot_somatic_mutation 0.46). Established ccRCC drug target.

Open Targets association 0.4566 (rank 13 of 1998). Tractability AB/OC/PR/SM, AB and SM Approved Drug. Many drugs incl. AXITINIB, CABOZANTINIB, PAZOPANIB, SORAFENIB, TIVOZANIB, LENVATINIB (APPROVAL/late stage), RAMUCIRUMAB (APPROVAL). Cell membrane receptor for VEGFA; angiogenesis. Convergence rank 21 (5 streams). Established ccRCC target (VEGFR).

Open Targets association 0.525 (rank 6 of 1998). Tractability AB/PR/SM (SM: Approved Drug). Drugs include RIDAFOROLIMUS (APPROVAL), GEDATOLISIB (PHASE_3), DACTOLISIB (PHASE_3), SAPANISERTIB (PHASE_2). Central regulator of growth; mTORC1 signalling. Established ccRCC target (mTOR inhibitors).

Open Targets overall association 0.3088 (rank 79 of 1998), no genetic/somatic score (ot_genetic 0.0, somatic 0.0), so support is omics/tractability driven; convergence rank 10 (4 streams). Tractability AB (Advanced Clinical), PR, SM. Drugs: GIRENTUXIMAB (PHASE_3), IODINE I 124 GIRENTUXIMAB (PHASE_2), SULTHIAME (PHASE_4), ETHOXZOLAMIDE (WITHDRAWAL). Cell membrane/microvillus membrane (antibody-accessible); HIF pathway; STRING partners HIF1A 0.972, EPAS1 0.923, ARNT 0.898. Strong imaging/antibody target and HIF-axis biomarker.

Open Targets association 0.389 (rank 30 of 1998); convergence rank 6 (5 streams, somatic 0.42). Tractability AB/OC/PR/SM. Drugs: CABOZANTINIB (APPROVAL), TEPOTINIB (APPROVAL), CAPMATINIB (PHASE_4), SAVOLITINIB (PHASE_3), TELISOTUZUMAB VEDOTIN (PHASE_3). Membrane receptor; PI3K/AKT and RAS signalling. Cabozantinib-class MET/VEGFR inhibition is established in ccRCC; MET itself partly tested.

Top of convergence ranking (rank 1, score 3.87, 5 streams; RNA log2FC 1.461, protein log2FC 1.062, CNV gain freq 0.255). Open Targets association 0.3049 (rank 90 of 1998), somatic 0.456. Drugs: AFATINIB (PHASE_4), RUSERONTINIB (PHASE_3), TESEVATINIB (PHASE_3), CETUXIMAB SAROTALOCAN (APPROVAL). Cell membrane. Tractable and druggable, but not an established ccRCC drug target (tractable-but-untested).

Convergence rank 4 (score 3.8042, 5 streams). Open Targets association 0.3017 (rank 100 of 1998), somatic 0.46. Drugs: PLERIXAFOR and MAVORIXAFOR (APPROVAL), BURIXAFOR (PHASE_2). Cell membrane chemokine receptor. Tractable, ccRCC use untested.

Convergence rank 11 (5 streams). Open Targets association 0.4265 (rank 23 of 1998), genetic 0.56. Tractability AB (Advanced Clinical), OC. Drugs: DULANERMIN, DROZITUMAB, TIGATUZUMAB, LEXATUMUMAB, CONATUMUMAB (all PHASE_2). Membrane death receptor (TRAIL-R2). Tractable but untested in ccRCC.

Convergence rank 5 (score 3.7768, 5 streams). Open Targets association 0.4532 (rank 16 of 1998), genetic component 0.73. Tractability AB and SM (High-Quality Pocket), no clinical drug. Cell membrane and secreted (accessible for antibody and biomarker use). Association-driven candidate, not drugged.

Convergence rank 16 (5 streams). Open Targets association 0.4049 (rank 24 of 1998), genetic 0.52. Tractability AB/PR/SM (Druggable Family, High-Quality Ligand), no clinical drug. Cell membrane/caveola; HDL clearance and class B scavenger pathways (lipid handling). Tractable but untested.

caveats: Open Targets overall score does not equal the genetics datatype used in the ranking; many top-ranked omics genes (CA9, CD74, FAS) have ot_genetic_association 0.
Drug stages are as returned by Open Targets and are not ccRCC-specific (e.g. EGFR, CXCR4 drugs are approved for other indications).
Some tractability or association evidence ids were not retrieved for EGFR drug beyond one id; STRING only run for CA9.
Evidence ids not verified with check_evidence_ids prior to this step beyond tool-returned values.

summary.text: Three kinds of candidates emerge when CPTAC tumor-versus-normal omics, the literature corpus and external knowledge are integrated. First, established ccRCC drug targets whose evidence is genetic and clinical rather than expression-based: HIF-2α (EPAS1, belzutifan approved), the VEGF receptor KDR (multiple approved tyrosine kinase inhibitors) and MTOR. Second, HIF-driven surface or secreted proteins with large, layer-concordant increases in tumors and an existing clinical modality: CA9 (girentuximab, phase 3) and CD70 (cusatuzumab and antibody–drug conjugates). Third, metabolic tissue biomarkers that capture the clear-cell phenotype (NDUFA4L2/COXFA4L2, PLIN2, ENO2, NNMT, SLC16A3) or the loss of proximal-tubule identity (ALDOB).

CA9 is the candidate with the most complete convergence. It is increased at RNA (log2FC 6.31), protein (2.27) and phosphoprotein level, RNA and protein agree across tumors (Spearman ρ 0.80), the literature supports CA9-targeted PET imaging, and an anti-CA9 antibody has reached phase 3. Its weakness is the absence of Open Targets germline or somatic genetic evidence, which lowers it to rank 10 in the deterministic score.

The deterministic ranking places EGFR, CD74, FAS, CXCR4 and PIGR at the top. These genes show modest but concordant expression changes and receive a uniform Open Targets somatic-mutation score that is not specific to ccRCC. Several of them are expressed by infiltrating immune cells (CXCR4, CD74). They are tractable but have little or no ccRCC-specific literature in this corpus, so they are presented as hypotheses rather than priorities.

omics.text: The CPTAC discovery cohort reproduces the canonical VHL–HIF biology. VHL lies on 3p, which is lost in 79 % of tumors, and the HIF targets CA9 and NDUFA4L2 (HGNC COXFA4L2) carry the largest tumor-versus-normal changes in the dataset (RNA log2FC 6.31 and 6.75; protein 2.27 and 3.77).

Beyond hypoxia, the proteome captures the metabolic rewiring of ccRCC. Glycolysis and lactate export rise (ENO2 protein log2FC 2.25; SLC16A3/MCT4 2.28), as do lipid-droplet formation (PLIN2 2.67) and NNMT (2.71). ALDOB falls (protein log2FC −2.27; RNA −7.03), marking the loss of proximal-tubule identity.

VHL and PBRM1 illustrate why expression-based convergence misses genetic drivers. Both are lost with 3p in about 80 % of tumors, yet their protein levels barely change (VHL log2FC −0.17; PBRM1 −0.27).

literature.text: Translational literature in this corpus is strongest for CA9 (tumor-cell enrichment with low normal-kidney expression and CA9-directed PET imaging) and for NDUFA4L2, which predicts poor survival and promotes glycolysis. Most other literature-supported candidates rest on single retrospective or bioinformatic studies.

The corpus contains contradictions that a single score would hide. MT1G is reported both as downregulated in tumors and as a marker of poor prognosis, and for PFKP increased expression in tumors coexists with a report linking low expression to worse survival.

external.text: Open Targets identifies the targets already exploited clinically in ccRCC: EPAS1 (belzutifan, approved), KDR (approved VEGFR inhibitors) and MTOR (approved rapalog). They rank 9, 13 and 6 of 1,998 targets associated with ccRCC.
MET combines omics support with strong druggability. It is increased in RNA, protein and phosphoprotein, and approved inhibitors exist (cabozantinib, already used in ccRCC, and tepotinib).

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge agree most clearly on CA9: all three agents independently selected it, and it is the only candidate with expression, literature and a late-stage clinical modality at once. CD70 and NDUFA4L2 follow, with strong omics and literature support but early or no clinical drugs.

The evidence streams disagree in systematic ways. The established drug targets (EPAS1, KDR, MTOR) have genetic and clinical support but weak bulk-expression changes. The top omics genes have little ccRCC literature. Immune-related genes in the ranking (CXCR4, CD74) may reflect infiltration rather than tumor-cell expression. Prioritization therefore requires judgment across streams, not a single score.

limitations.text: Single discovery cohort (CPTAC, 110 tumors) without independent validation; bulk tissue comparisons mix tumor-cell and microenvironment signals.
Somatic mutation data were outside the data scope, so mutational drivers (VHL, PBRM1, SETD2, BAP1, KDM5C) are captured only through 3p loss and Open Targets.
The literature corpus has ~320 abstracts and was searched for the top omics genes, so absence of literature for a gene is not evidence of absence.
Open Targets assigns a uniform somatic-mutation score (0.456) to many cancer-census genes, which inflates the genetics stream for genes without ccRCC-specific mutation evidence.
Copy-number frequencies below 0.3 are reported in agent statements but have no evidence record in the graph.

Drug stages are reported for any indication, not specifically for ccRCC. LLM steps (relation extraction, agent analyses, this narrative) are not bit-reproducible; their outputs are saved and every statement was verified against the graph.

targets.rationale: Largest concordant multi-layer increase (RNA log2FC 6.31, protein 2.27, ρ 0.80), membrane enzyme, CA9-PET literature, girentuximab phase 3. Ranked 10 by the deterministic score only because it lacks germline or somatic genetic evidence.
HIF-2α, the direct effector of VHL loss; belzutifan approved. Little bulk-expression change, so the omics stream underrates it.
VEGFR2, the backbone of ccRCC therapy, with many approved inhibitors; Open Targets rank 13.
Surface ligand up in RNA (log2FC 4.46) and protein (2.42) with the highest RNA–protein concordance among candidates (ρ 0.84); antibody and ADC programs exist.
Up in RNA, protein and phosphoprotein; approved inhibitors including cabozantinib, already used in ccRCC.
Established ccRCC pathway with an approved rapalog; Open Targets rank 6. Driven by pathway activation, not expression change.
NDUFA4L2: the largest RNA and protein increase in the cohort (log2FC 6.75 and 3.77) and literature linking it to poor survival and glycolysis. Excellent tissue biomarker; no drug yet.
MCT4 lactate exporter up in RNA (log2FC 3.44) and protein (2.28); a membrane transporter consistent with the glycolytic phenotype, a plausible metabolic target.
Lipid-droplet protein up in protein (log2FC 2.67); validated in an IHC diagnostic panel in the literature.
Glycolytic enzyme up in protein (log2FC 2.25), reported as a diagnostic and prognostic marker.
Strongest decrease (RNA log2FC −7.03; protein −2.27): a negative tissue biomarker of proximal-tubule identity loss, not a target.

Top of the deterministic ranking (modest but concordant increases, 7p gain, tractable), but no ccRCC literature in the corpus and only a non-specific somatic score: a hypothesis to test, not a priority.
